incident-bot: [ALERT] High 429 rate detected for tenant=lynx-enterprise (dedicated pool: dp-lynx-7) · 199 requests/minute error spike · https://redwood.internal/alerts/ALRT-1999
Alex: paging oncall, I'm oncall for infra this shift. seeing customer-reported 429s, alert says dedicated pool saturated.
Miguel: jumping in — I'm SRE oncall. can you paste the error snippet from the gateway logs?
Alex: paste from last 5m:
```
2026-03-14T21:12:03Z gateway - tenant=lynx-enterprise status=429 route=/v1/generate tokens=12.3 seq_len=512 reason=rate_limited
2026-03-14T21:12:04Z gateway - tenant=lynx-enterprise status=429 route=/v1/embeddings tokens=0.8 reason=burst_limit
```
Eve: CS got a ticket from Lynx — they said their inference jobs spiked after a batch import. Customer is asking for immediate relief.
Jordan: Account here — they have an enterprise contract with a negotiated burst clause but it requires ops approval. I can sign off if SRE confirms mitigation plan.
Miguel: quick check of pool dp-lynx-7 metrics: GPUs at 99% util, backlog increasing, autoscaler didn’t kick (min=max configured). Looks like dedicated pool was sized for steady load, not bursts.
Lina: can we redirect noncritical routes to fallback model? e.g., reroute /embeddings -> lower-tier model to reduce token pressure?
Miguel: good idea. short-term plan: 1) apply temporary rate override for tenant to lift 429s for 15m, 2) add routing rule to redirect embeddings to emb-medium for next 30m, 3) notify customer and monitor. Need an ops exec to apply override.
Jen: OpsBot has a runbook for emergency quota lifts: `#runbook/emergency-rate-exemption`. Steps require ticket and approver header. I can enact once Jordan posts approval.
Jordan: approved for 15m emergency lift. Jordan: +1 to proceed, account approves.
Alex: executing routing change now — applying traffic-split rule:
```
PATCH /config/routing/dp-lynx-7
{
  "rules": [
    {"match": "/embeddings", "model": "embed-medium", "weight": 1.0}
  ]
}
```
OpsBot: routing change accepted, config version v20260314-0823.
Miguel: I'm about to run the emergency lift. command:
```
POST /admin/tenants/lynx-enterprise/overrides
{ "type": "burst_rate", "duration_min": 15, "reason": "customer import spike", "approved_by": "Jordan" }
```
Miguel: override applied — tenant quota increased by 3x for 15m. Monitoring tail.
Eve: Lina told Lynx support: "We've applied a temporary burst relief and routed embeddings to a lower-cost model. We'll keep you posted."
Alex: metrics update 5m after changes: 429 rate dropped to 3/min, GPU util 82%, request latency steady.
Lina: customer confirmed they see success for the import and reduced errors.
Jordan: logging approval and CIAM sign-off. I'll update the account case.
Miguel: leaving the override to expire automatically. I'll keep an eye for regression. Post-incident TODOs: - followup sizing for dp-lynx-7, - formalize burst clause automation, - add alert for autoscaler misconfiguration.
Eve: assigning postmortem owner: Eve -> will coordinate with Eng/Account; target doc by EOD tomorrow.
Alex: handoff to next oncall (Miguel -> Jen): Jen, you'll get a followup ping when override expires (~15m).
OpsBot: override will auto-expire at 1999999050 (approx).
Jen: ack. marking incident resolved in channel once override removed and customer stable.
Miguel: final note: no customer data exposure, only rate/throughput. closing thread after confirmation. :white_check_mark:
